## RQ2 — Immune-related signatures

Are 18-gene T-cell–inflamed GEP (see D6; Ayers et al. (2017)) associated with treatment response?<https://www.jci.org/articles/view/91190>

Reference: 10.1172/JCI91190

-   Suggested tasks: Identify the 18 genes included in the published T-cell–inflamed GEP and examine their expression in the dataset.

-   Calculate a T-cell–inflamed GEP score for each patient.

-   Investigate whether patients with higher GEP scores are more likely to respond to anti-PD-L1 treatment.

-   Interpret the biological significance of your findings and discuss why a high T-cell–inflamed GEP score does not necessarily guarantee treatment response

```{r}
packages <- c("immunedeconv", 
              "ggplot2",
              "limma",
              "tidyverse")
missing <- packages[!vapply(packages,
                            requireNamespace,
                            logical(1),
                            quietly=TRUE)]
if(length(missing)) 
  stop("Install missing packages: ",
       paste(missing,collapse=", "))

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(immunedeconv);
  library(ggplot2);
  library(limma);
  library(tidyverse)})
```

```{r}
genes_18 <- c(
  "CD27", "CD274", "CCL5",
  "CD276", "CD8A", "CMKLR1",
  "CXCL9", "CXCR6", "HLA-DQA1", "HLA-DRB1", "HLA-E",
  "IDO1", "LAG3", "NKG7", "PDCD1LG2", "PSMB10", "STAT1", "TIGIT"
)

missing_GEP <- setdiff(genes_18,rownames(expr))
cat("GEP genes present:",
    length(genes_18)-length(missing_GEP),
    "of",length(genes_18),
    "\n")
```

```{r}
plot_response_boxplot <- function(data,variable,title) {
  ggplot(data,aes(x=Response,y=.data[[variable]])) +
    geom_boxplot(outlier.shape=NA,alpha=.3) +
    geom_jitter(width=.12,alpha=.65,size=1.5) +
    labs(title=title,x="Response class",y=variable)+theme_minimal()
}
plot_association <- function(data,x,y,title) {
  ggplot(data,aes(x=.data[[x]],y=.data[[y]]))+
    geom_point(alpha=.7)+geom_smooth(method="lm",se=FALSE,color="steelblue")+
    labs(title=title,x=x,y=y)+theme_minimal()
}
spearman_test <- function(x,y) cor.test(x,y,method="spearman",exact=FALSE,use="complete.obs")
```
